track.title: SPIFFE node and terminal security matrix
track.purpose: Preserve the exact identity, authorization, lifecycle, and environment-gate context needed to resume the SPIFFE security matrix without re-investigating settled architecture.
track.operating_mode: Kind validates workload identity and authorization separation; external-host attestation and production SPIRE operations remain explicit prerequisites.
track.active_scope: Build and run the kind-capable matrix cases, preserve exact fail-closed expectations, and keep external-host acceptance separate.
track.current_objective: Prepare the SPIFFE node and terminal security matrix from committed architecture and shadow integration while preventing kind evidence from being presented as external-host or production proof.
decisions: SPIFFE authenticates workloads; OIDC/IAM, signed tasks, allocation state, quarantine, and single-use terminal capabilities remain authorization authorities.
blockers: OPS-SPIRE-EXTERNAL-NODE-ATTESTATION-PILOT-001 is blocked, so external-host clone, replay, attestor, HA, and recovery acceptance cannot be closed from kind alone.
next_actions: Implement and run dependency-safe kind matrix cases; resume external-host cases only when the disposable attestation environment is available.

pages.title: SPIFFE Node and Terminal Identity
pages.excerpt: SPIFFE Node and Terminal Identity The durable identity contract uses SPIFFE IDs and the SPIFFE Workload API for node-agent-to-platform and node-agent-to-terminal-gateway channels. SPIRE is the preferred reference implementation and pilot candidate, not yet the unconditional production implementation. pages.title: Current state
pages.excerpt: Current State Human identity and role authorization remain in OIDC, IAM, and policy. Terminal access requires an API-minted, allocation-bound, single-use capability. Workload identity does not replace that authorization. The node agent pulls signed typed tasks, executes allowlisted operations, and reports correlated results. pages.title: Node Agent Lifecycle
pages.excerpt: Node Agent Lifecycle The node agent is the constrained execution boundary between control-plane intent and host-side effects. The control plane registers versioned operation definitions, enforces authorization and policy, schedules signed tasks, and mints short-lived task-bound credentials.
